newsitem.title: USA: Sun hits fourth straight high ahead of Q4.
newsitem.headline: Sun hits fourth straight high ahead of Q4.

text.p: Shares of Sun Microsystems Inc Thursday rose to an all-time high for the fourth consecutive day, at one point showing a gain for the week so far of 8-3/4, or more than 22 percent.
Wall Street analysts expects a solid set of results for Sun's fiscal year ended June 30, with fourth quarter First Call consensus earnings estimates at $0.58 a share.

"Surprisingly enough there has been no whisper number," said one prominent analyst. "The air has been bone dry, in terms of a whisper number, but certainly it would be nice to see a comforting number to go along with it."
Another analyst said the company has in the past managed its results by reinvesting any excess gross profit margin back into its business, rather than reporting a "blowout" quarter.
Shares of Sun vaulted as high as $47-7/8 in Thursday trading ahead of the results, due after the market close, up more than 22 percent from last Friday's close of 39-1/8.
In the final hour of trading it had retreated to $46, up $1 on the day, with volume topping 13 million shares.

Since April 25, the stock has risen more than 75 percent to Thursday's peak trading level, although the share has had a history in recent quarters of running up ahead of results, then slipping lower after the earnings reports.

"My guess is its going to be a couple of pennies above, maybe two or three pennies," over the per-share consensus estimates," said C.B. Lee of Sutro & Co, who has a $0.59 a share estimate for Sun. He sees revenue growth "in the high teens" compared with its record fourth quarter revenues of $2.02 billion, a year ago, when it posted a 22 percent rise.
The year-ago earnings per share were $0.43 on a split adjusted basis.

Analysts are also looking closely at backlog figures and at the company's book-to-bill ratio -- Lee expects this to be better than one, meaning that the company is booking more orders than the number of shipments it has made.

Although Sun does not break down its results by business, Lee is expecting a 30 percent sequential rise in server sales, and he expects margins could be above the third quarter's levels of around 50.2 percent.
J.P. Morgan analyst Daniel Kunstler said he expects the company could somewhat exceed his revenue estimate of $2.32 billion, which would be up 15 percent from a year ago.
Kunstller said he has heard "very favorable things" about the demand for Sun's server products.
